strict.criterion: A machine passes the specific two-hour, multi-judge protocol in the Kurzweil–Kapor wager.
strict.rationale: The 2029 wager deadline is still ahead. The located evidence does not document a completed pass under that contract. Five-minute conversational studies are a different protocol.

evidence.title: Long Bets #1 — Kapor/Kurzweil Turing-test agreement
evidence.note: Kapor takes the NO side; Kurzweil takes the opposing side. Detailed test conditions belong to this contract, not to every generic use of “Turing test.”

evidence.title: Large Language Models Pass the Turing Test — Jones and Bergen
evidence.note: Five-minute experimental protocol. GPT-4.5 with a humanlike persona was judged human in 73% of the reported comparisons. Not the two-hour Long Bets protocol.

broader.criterion: A machine passes a demanding multi-turn human-imitation test comparable in spirit to the Kurzweil–Kapor wager by 2029.
broader.rationale: The 2029 wager deadline is still ahead and Long Bets has not adjudicated a win. Jones and Bergen's 2025 study showed GPT-4.5 judged human in 73% of five-minute conversations—strong partial progress—but a five-minute chat does not fulfill a two-hour adversarial wager three years before its deadline.
changedConditions: Recognizes short-format conversational imitation tests as strong partial progress while waiting for 2029 or formal adjudication
